title: Recap Everything So Far
sheet: cheatsheet for each week (the Study Desk shows every week)
footer: Two new questions for every topic done so far: weeks 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 9 (BST) and 11 (union-find). New numbers, not the practice quiz. Do this after the five new topics, then once more on exam eve.

qs.p: Which of these grows the fastest as n gets very large?
qs.ex: From slowest to fastest: n log n, n², n³, 2ⁿ. Anything with n in the power (like 2ⁿ) beats every fixed power of n.
Keep the fastest-growing term (3n²) and drop its number: n². Θ means exactly that growth.

qs.p: Merge sort has the recurrence T(n) = 2T(n/2) + n. What does the Master Theorem give?
qs.ex: a = 2, b = 2, so n to the power log base 2 of 2 is n¹ = n. f(n) = n is the same size, which is Case 2: multiply by log n, giving Θ(n log n).

qs.p: Binary search has the recurrence T(n) = T(n/2) + 1. What is its running time?
qs.ex: a = 1, b = 2, so n to the power log base 2 of 1 is n⁰ = 1. f(n) = 1 is the same size, Case 2: Θ(1 times log n) = Θ(log n).

qs.p: What is the running time of BFS on a graph stored as an adjacency list?
qs.ex: Every vertex joins the queue once and every edge is looked at once (or twice if undirected), so O(V + E). O((V + E) log V) is Dijkstra.

qs.p: A graph has some negative edge weights (but no negative cycles). Which algorithm should find the shortest paths?
qs.ex: Dijkstra can give wrong answers with negative edges, and BFS ignores weights. Bellman-Ford handles negative edges.

qs.p: What is the length of the longest increasing subsequence of 4, 10, 4, 3, 8, 9?
qs.ex: L = 1, 2, 1, 1, 2, 3. For 8: the smaller numbers to its left (4, 4, 3) all have L 1, so 2. For 9: 8 has L 2, so 3. The answer is the biggest L: 3 (for example 4, 8, 9).

qs.p: An edit distance box has up = 2, left = 3, diagonal = 1, and its two letters are different. What goes in the box?
qs.ex: up 2 + 1 = 3, left 3 + 1 = 4, diagonal 1 + 1 = 2 (different letters, so plus 1). Smallest is 2.

qs.p: A graph has edges A–B (1), B–C (2), A–C (3) and C–D (4). Kruskal's algorithm runs on it. Which edge is rejected, and what is the MST weight?
qs.ex: A–B 1 accept, B–C 2 accept, A–C 3 reject (A and C are already joined through B), C–D 4 accept. Total 1 + 2 + 4 = 7.

qs.p: Activities [0, 6), [1, 3), [3, 5), [5, 8). Which does the earliest finish time rule pick?
qs.ex: Sort by finish: [1, 3) finishes 3, [3, 5) finishes 5, [0, 6) finishes 6, [5, 8) finishes 8. Pick [1, 3). [3, 5) starts at 3, pick. [0, 6) starts at 0, skip. [5, 8) starts at 5, pick. 3 activities.

qs.p: An augmenting path has residual room 6, 2 and 9 on its three edges. How much flow can be pushed along it?
qs.ex: The bottleneck is the smallest room on the path: 2.

qs.p: An edge has label 4/7 (flow 4, capacity 7). What are its residual capacities?
qs.ex: Forward room = capacity minus flow = 7 − 4 = 3. Reverse room = the flow = 4.

qs.p: The keys 15, 10, 20, 12 are inserted into an empty BST in that order. Where is 12?
qs.ex: 15 is the root. 10 goes left of 15. 20 goes right of 15. 12: smaller than 15 so go left to 10, bigger than 10 so go right: empty, so 12 is the right child of 10.

qs.p: In the preorder walk of any BST, which key comes first?
qs.ex: Preorder is root, left, right, so the root is always written first. In postorder the root is last. Inorder starts with the smallest key.

qs.p: Union by rank joins two roots that both have rank 2. What is the rank of the new root?
qs.ex: A tie: one root goes under the other, and the new root's rank goes up by 1, from 2 to 3. Different ranks never raise a rank.

qs.p: FIND-SET(x) is run with path compression. What happens to the ranks?
opts: Every rank on the path drops to 0
The root's rank goes up by 1
Ranks are recalculated as exact heights
qs.ex: Path compression only changes parent arrows: every node on the find path points straight at the root. Ranks stay the same.
